UK Documents: Authorities and Price Bands

Every document in the United Kingdom comes from a different office. This hub lists all six with the office that issues it and the observed band, so you can pick the right page before you open a chat.

Price bands differ by document by an order of magnitude and the checks differ completely. Read the office column before the price column, because the office tells you what the document is and the price only tells you what a seller hopes to get for it.

UK documents: the six offices

Issuing office by document.
DocumentOfficeObserved
PassportHM Passport Office140–500 GBP
Driving Licencethe DVLA in Great Britain and the DVA in Northern Ireland80–320 GBP
ID Cardthe DVLA or a PASS accredited card scheme70–260 GBP
Green Cardthe Home Office280–950 GBP
VisaUK Visas and Immigration120–480 GBP
Residence Permitthe Home Office250–800 GBP

Two checks specific to the United Kingdom

  • Check the DVLA or DVA hologram and confirm the licence number encodes the surname, which is the numbering rule.
  • Confirm the issue date on the photocard against the record the seller shows for it.

Local red flag

  • A driving licence that uses the American spelling on the card face.
